I could only read the SoundGuys roundup. Runner's World and WIRED wouldn't load, so I haven't read their picks. The search snippets also don't show the Shokz and Bose reviews, so I can't say how those models compare. The notes below come from SoundGuys.

**Top picks for running**

- **Best clip-on for runners: HUAWEI FreeClip 2, $199.99.** SoundGuys recommends it most directly for running. It's light, has an IP57 water-resistance rating, and keeps you aware of your surroundings. It's expensive, and the fit affects the sound. [SoundGuys roundup](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- **Best budget pick: Soundcore AeroFit 2.** It has four-position adjustable ear hooks, an IP55 rating, multipoint pairing, and a customizable EQ. The touch controls are very sensitive. One owner reported about 6 hours of battery against the 10 hours claimed.
  - SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon.
  - A third-party deal page, Dealectric, says code AFSC20 brings it to $104 from $129.99 at Soundcore's US store. That page says it tested the code on 2026-10-22, and I haven't verified it. The Amazon price looks lower, so compare before you buy. [Dealectric link](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- **Good all-rounder: Nothing Ear (Open), about $99 on Amazon ($149 MSRP).** It has strong bass for an open design, long battery life, a parametric EQ, and an IP54 rating. SoundGuys describes it as suited to athletes. [SoundGuys roundup](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Others**

- **Sony LinkBuds Open, about $158.** It lasts about 9.5 hours and supports multipoint pairing. [SoundGuys roundup](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- **Apple AirPods 4, about $139.** They're comfortable for many people, but the fit is one-size with no swappable tips. [SoundGuys roundup](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 and Bose Ultra Open Earbuds**

I couldn't read the Shokz or Bose reviews, so I can't judge them. Both appear in the results, and Runner's World reports that almost every NYC marathoner wore Shokz. You can compare them on [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946) and read the [WIRED review of the OpenRun Pro 2](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/).

**My suggestion:** Get the AeroFit 2 if you want the best value. Get the FreeClip 2 if you want a more premium, lightweight clip-on. Choose a bone-conduction model like the Shokz if you want the most secure fit.

If you tell me your budget, I can narrow it down.

**Top picks** (prices are the Amazon prices listed on the page; MSRP in parentheses)

1. **Nothing Ear (Open): $99 ($149 MSRP)**
   - *Pros:* Strong bass for an open design, long battery life, good controls, a parametric EQ in the companion app, IP54 rating.
   - *Cons:* The page names no major drawbacks. Its text gives the price as $149.99 in one place.

2. **Apple AirPods 4: $138.86 ($119 MSRP)**
   - *Pros:* Comfortable fit for many users, H2 chip, Adaptive EQ, IP54 rating, Apple ecosystem features.
   - *Cons:* One-size fit with no swappable tips, so trying them on first matters. Owner reviews are mixed, with one describing the treble as too bright.

3. **Sony LinkBuds Open: $157.95 ($229.99 MSRP)**
   - *Pros:* About 9.5 hours of battery, Auto Switch multipoint, LE Audio/LC3 support, background music effect, IPX4-equivalent protection.
   - *Cons:* Shares the usual open-earbud sound tradeoffs. The page lists its price as $199.99 in the body text, which conflicts with the listing.

4. **Anker Soundcore AeroFit 2: $79.99 ($99.99 MSRP), best budget pick**
   - *Pros:* Four-position adjustable ear hooks, IP55 rating, multipoint, 23 EQ presets, and a customizable graphic EQ.
   - *Cons:* Touch controls are very sensitive. One owner reports about 6 hours of real-world battery versus the 10 hours claimed.

5. **HUAWEI FreeClip 2: $199.99 (same MSRP), clip-on pick**
   - *Pros:* Lightweight, either earbud works in either ear, IP57 rating, strong battery life, and above-average bass when positioned well.
   - *Cons:* Expensive. They block no outside noise, which is the intended design, and fit strongly affects sound.

**Best for running:** The page most directly recommends the **HUAWEI FreeClip 2** for runners, citing its light weight, IP57 water resistance, and awareness of surroundings. If you want a cheaper option, the **AeroFit 2** offers a secure fit and IP55 protection for sweaty workouts. The **Nothing Ear (Open)** is also described as suited to athletes.
